A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualXDA work. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable matching, including retained Appendices A–H and the added Appendix I in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision-model evaluations, sparsity and surrogate-faithfulness analyses, and XDA case studies and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendices F–H.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Llama-3.2-1B experiments on AG News, reporting resource consumption and shortcut-detection outcomes in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The SVM surrogate, DualDA attribution equations, LRP-based XDA procedure and concept decomposition in Appendix H are retained. Applying DualDA to a language model does not introduce a different attribution algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds AG News topic classification and a keyword-induced shortcut scenario using Llama-3.2-1B. This substantially extends the evaluated coverage from vision to language while retaining MNIST, CIFAR-10, AwA2 and ImageNet experiments.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same eight baselines: LiSSA, Arnoldi, EK-FAC, TracIn, GradDot, GradCos, TRAK and Representer Points. The new language-model resource comparison reuses EK-FAC; it does not introduce a new comparator or remove one from an existing experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds resource measurements with metric-specific EK-FAC batch sizes and a shortcut protocol using 4,000 training samples, 20% shortcut injection and 1,000 manipulated test samples. Section 4.4 adds cumulative absolute-attribution analysis. These extend the evaluation procedures without revising the retained vision protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds a controlled language shortcut study examining detection success across sparsity settings, plus an absolute-attribution sparsity analysis. The vision ablations, surrogate sparsification tests and concept case study remain; the earlier sign-separated sparsity analysis moves to Appendix F.7.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed and statistical uncertainty reporting are unchanged. The caching-time range in Table I.1 describes variation across three C settings, not confidence intervals or repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Appendix I adds substantial new results, including 0.04 seconds per explanation for DualDA versus more than 4,345 seconds for EK-FAC, and a reported shortcut AUPRC of 0.88. However, Figure I.1 plots discovered shortcuts against queried samples, leaving that metric attribution unclear. Figure 5 adds absolute-attribution findings; the original vision benchmark results are retained.

T1.justification: The optimization problems, attribution formulas, Theorem 3.1, derivations in Appendices A–C and concept-decomposition mathematics in Appendix H remain unchanged. More explicit domain notation in Definition 2.1 and equivalent notation changes do not alter the formal content.

C1.justification: The conclusion removes the broad assertion of real-world applicability to state-of-the-art models and qualifies the novelty claim about training/test interaction explanations with the inference context of a trained model. The principal DualDA/XDA contributions and headline vision speedup claims remain.

C2.justification: Where v2 mainly discusses SVM training bottlenecks, v3's new Section 6 explicitly addresses classification-only demonstrations, incomplete foundation-model evaluation and the absence of quantitative XDA validation. Sections 4.2 and F.3 also recommend C = 10^-3 for convolutional image classifiers while explaining why other settings require retuning.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds hardware, model/data sources, SVM training times and EK-FAC batch-setting details. Section 4.3 changes the implementation-access statement to code being available upon acceptance, although the abstract retains the repository link and says code is available. This creates conflicting availability wording; actual repository access cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Llama 3 and AG News and removes the SemanticLens, PSVM and ThunderSVM references. These are limited citation and positioning changes; the main organization and comparison of data-attribution approaches remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the title and abstract, edits introductory and concluding passages, rewrites the sparsity discussion and separates Limitations & Future Work from the conclusion. Cross-references are also revised. Most methodological, theoretical and experimental exposition retains its structure and wording.

P2.justification: v3 adds an absolute-attribution Figure 5, Table I.1 and Figure I.1. The original Figure 5 is retained as Figure F.9, and other existing graphics remain unchanged despite relocation and page reflow. Captions and figure placement receive limited revisions.

improvement.justification: The new language-model resource measurements provide empirical support for scalability that v2 presented as future work, while the expanded limitations and hyperparameter guidance improve interpretation. These offer a modest net gain. The preliminary study remains narrow, its shortcut plot does not match the claimed precision–recall presentation, and conflicting code-availability statements weaken reporting.
